REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MARCH 9, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
SIERRA ROOM - CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING ARTS
18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Sierra Room subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

PERFORMING ARTS, 18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Dustin Parker, Concordia Lutheran Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Pee Wee Division Youth Basketball – Lakers.

4.  Roll Call

  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Joe Pak expressed concern regarding the impact of the recent inclement weather on a tree

  OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS EXTENDING A MORATORIUM ON THE
  ESTABLISHMENT AND/OR OPERATION OF TATTOO ESTABLISHMENTS, AND

8B.  Review and consideration to request for City Council direction regarding the City’s existing
  transportation services, the Cerritos on Wheels fixed-route service and the Dial-A-Ride
  demand response service (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sabrina Chan, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8B.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and the public comments period.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record. Full-text copies of submitted written
  correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Steven Hsieh expressed support for maintaining the Cerritos on Wheels (COW) fixed route
  service and suggested eco-friendly, autonomous transportation systems.

  Murali Vasudevan expressed concern regarding the potential purchase of electric public
  transit and suggested alternatives for Cerritos public transit for residents and students.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period and public hearing closed.

  MAIN MOTION (HELD PENDING):  It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by
  Johnson, to approve:

  1. Options 1A and 2A as detailed in the associated agenda report for this item, detailed
  as follows and as amended to:

  a. Direct the consultant to evaluate the feasibility and costs associated with
  connectivity to Cerritos business centers; and

  b. Direct staff to notify ABC Unified School District administration of the City’s
  upcoming comprehensive review of the fixed-route COW and demand response
  Dial-A-Ride programs and that a potential outcome of the review could include
  modification or discontinuation of the programs (COUNCIL).

  City Council and staff discussion and deliberation ensued on the main motion.

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION (WITHDRAWN): It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by
  Barrows, as amended, to approve Options 1B and 2B as detailed in the associated agenda
  report for this item (COUNCIL).

  Upon City Council discussion and deliberation on the substitute motion, additional
  amendments were developed, rendering the substitute motion moot. The substitute
  motion was withdrawn by Solanki and Barrows.

  MAIN MOTION (ADOPTED): It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Johnson, to
  approve:

  1. Options 1A and 2A listed in the associated agenda report, detailed as follows and as
  amended to:

  a. Continue providing fixed-route COW and demand response Dial-A-Ride services on
  a month-to-month basis upon expiration of the existing agreements on June 30,
  2023; and

  b. Solicit proposals for a consultant to conduct an analysis of the existing services for
  the purpose of formulating recommendations on how best to improve operational
  efficiency and effectiveness system-wide, and to aid in the selection of new
  contractors for the continuation of services. Such analysis shall include the
  formulation of recommendations related to the following:

  2. Dial-A-Ride service areas and operational hours; and

  4. Feasibility and costs associated with greater connectivity to City business and
